title: Pilot pitch sampler for platform ops
content:
Overview:
This doc is a compact sampler (3 micro-decks + one-page battlecard) for platform-focused pilots. Goal: give SEs and field ops a very short set of slides + one-pager they can braindump into a 10–15 minute intro with an ops audience, then hand off a repeatable checklist for a week-long pilot. Not a final deck — intentionally terse, with speaker notes and suggested A/B variants.

Context and constraints (notes to self):
- Primary audience: platform engineering, infra teams evaluating Dedicated or Private deployments.
- Key buying signals: need for predictable throughput, data isolation, SLA, and KMS integration.
- Typical pilot length: 3–7 days staging -> 1–3 week production validation.
- Risk appetite: medium; customer often wants reproducible perf numbers + fallback story.

Micro-deck A: 10-slide rapid run (ops-first)
Slide 1: Title + TL;DR
  Speaker note: "We’ll cover how Redwood reduces token cost while keeping predictable latency and a safety net for spikes."
Slide 2: Why predictable serving matters (concrete metric)
  Bullet: P50 vs P95 latency, token cost per 1M tokens, cost delta with caching.
  Note: add example numbers from pilot account; replace placeholders.
Slide 3: Deployment choices (hosted / dedicated / private) – ops checklist
  Note: highlight network requirements and KMS/hybrid connectivity.
Slide 4: Routing & fallback policy (how requests fail gracefully)
  Note: quick diagram: primary -> canary -> fallback model -> throttle queue.
Slide 5: Observability snapshot (what we’ll measure)
  Bullets: per-route latency, token breakdown, KV-cache hit rate, error types.
Slide 6: Quick demo plan (1st-day smoke, 3rd-day scale test)
Slide 7: Pilot acceptance criteria (3 items)
  - P95 under X ms for steady-state traffic
  - Cost below Y tokens per 1k prompts vs baseline
  - No data egress outside approved VPC
Slide 8: Common ops objections + answers (see battlecard)
Slide 9: Next steps and contact
Slide 10: Appendix: minimal infra diagram

Micro-deck B: 6-slide reliability-first (for SRE leads)
Slide 1: Title: Reliability-first contract
Slide 2: SLOs and failover mechanics (concrete examples)
Slide 3: Canary & rollback policy (how we run canaries with real traffic)
Slide 4: Capacity planning quick math (how to estimate reserved GPU needs)
  Note: include simple formula: requests-per-second * tokens-per-request * concurrency factor -> required GPU seconds.
Slide 5: On-call and incident playbook excerpt
Slide 6: Runbook handoff checklist

Micro-deck C: 8-slide cost-econ sampler (for CTO / finance partner)
Slide 1: Title + headline (cost predictability wins)
Slide 2: Unit economics: host vs dedicated vs private (example numbers)
Slide 3: Batching & caching levers + expected % cost reduction
Slide 4: Quantization/precision tradeoffs (quality vs cost)
Slide 5: Pilot ROI projection (3-month outlook)
Slide 6: Billing and observability (how they see token spend)
Slide 7: Procurement checkpoints (contracts, reserved capacity)
Slide 8: Call-to-action: proposal + SOW template link

One-page battlecard: pilot ops quick reference (single sheet)
Header: Pilot ops quick-reference — <customer name>
Left column: 60s elevator for platform lead:
  - "Redwood provides a consistent API across hosted/dedicated/private so you can pilot in-cloud then consume dedicated capacity without refactor."
  - Key metrics to ask for: P95 latency, throughput (rps), cache hit rate, token cost per 1k prompts.
Middle column: Quick objection-response (ops audience)
  Objection: "We need total control over keys and network."
    Answer: "Private deployment supports customer KMS and VPC-only control plane; we can whiteboard the network flow and KMS integration plan during kick-off."
  Objection: "We cannot risk silent model drift or regressions."
    Answer: "We run evals tied to your prompt-set and set regression alerts before enabling canary traffic. Add a rollback rule in rollout policy."
  Objection: "GPU costs are unpredictable."
    Answer: "We provide conservative throughput profiles per model and a dedicated commit path with burst capability you can dial down/up."
Right column: Quick pilot checklist (day-by-day)
  Day 0: Account & IAM setup, KMS test, network tunnel validation.
  Day 1: Smoke test with synthetic traffic, observe P50/P95.
  Day 2: KV/prefix caching validation; measure hit rates.
  Day 3: Real traffic soak at 10% baseline.
  Day 4: Scale test to 50% of expected peak.
  Day 5: Debrief & sign-off criteria review.

Sample SE scripts (30–60s lines):
- "If you're evaluating for dedicated capacity, the quickest way to reduce token spend is prefix caching for repeated context and switching to a quantized model for background tasks."
- "Our canary flow will start at 1% traffic, double every 30 minutes while checking quality gates — we roll back on first regression alert."

Pilot success metrics (what ops cares about):
- Latency: P95 < target (customer-specific)
- Stability: error rate < 0.1% during soak
- Cost: token spend delta vs baseline < agreed threshold
- Observability: dashboards and tracing connected to customer telemetry

Rollout red flags (call these out explicitly):
- KV cache hit rate < 20% during expected workload -> re-check prompt templating
- Burst patterns cause queueing -> consider reserved capacity or concurrency limit
- Third-party rate limits (upstreams) not accounted for -> mock them during scale test

Open questions / placeholders (to fill per-customer):
- Expected avg tokens per call (we need sample payloads)
- Peak concurrency and typical RPS windows (timezone effects)
- Security requirements: do they require HSM-backed KMS?
- Procurement timeline / preferred contract length

Quick appendix: links to artifacts to attach to pilot email
- Pre-built CloudFormation / Terraform snippets (link placeholder CONF-1223)
- Minimal ingest script (python) for synthetic tests (GH PR link above)
- Sample SLO template and sign-off form (JIRA-OPS-789)

Notes to SEs (informal):
- Keep <customer> deck to 8 slides max for execs. Use the 10-slide ops-deck only for the tech kickoff.
- Try variant A (ops-first) on first call; if buyer is SRE-heavy, swap in reliability-first.
- Use the battlecard column answers verbatim when pressed for time.
- TODO: get up-to-date throughput numbers for our recent dedicated 8xA100 SKU (ask infra team).

Action items / next steps:
- (Maya) Create the short deck templates in Google Slides from these notes (target: 2024-10-02).
- (Diego) Add the terraform snippets to the pilot-kits repo and link in the email template.
- (Aisha) Draft SOW checklist for reserved capacity pilots.
- (Omar) Run a rehearsal with two SEs and record the 10-minute ops pitch; capture common Qs.

Versioning notes: this is v0.1 sampler — meant to iterate quickly based on field feedback. Keep it short, lightweight, and easy to copy/paste into customer emails.

Unpolished brainstorm fragments (leave in — useful for future edits):
- "what if we offered a 48-hour 'rush' pilot that auto-rolls to dedicated during spike windows?"
- metrics card: show sample token billing for a customer with 250k monthly active prompts; compare host vs dedicated vs private with 10%/30%/50% caching rates.
- maybe a two-column quick visual: left = latency-focused, right = cost-focused, with recommended deployment for each.

End of doc.
